content.thinking:
I need to design a lava golem standing roughly 2.4 meters tall, styled in a Genshin Impact-inspired cel aesthetic with dark basalt ink tones, molten orange-gold glow seams, and gold filigree trim accents befitting a Pyro elemental look.

Now I'm planning the skeleton: hips rooted around y=1.05 with a spine chain rising through chest, neck, head, and jaw, plus arms with shoulder-elbow-wrist-finger joints and legs with hip-knee-ankle-toe joints, aiming for a rich but manageable rig that avoids risky API calls.

Planning torso coordinates and chain structure...

Working out radius functions for the torso taper, shoulder pauldrons, and neck-to-head joint placement...

Still defining joints and parts...

Planning fingers as short three-point curling chains per hand, grabbing the tip joint from the arm chain as the wrist parent, and figuring out world coordinates for the hand center to position them correctly.

Finishing the four-finger offsets with thumb, then giving fingers tapered basalt segments with dark clawed tips. Now I'm setting up the leg chains—hip, knee, ankle joints with forward bend direction and matching foot/toe placement so the pose reads anatomically correct.

For feet I'll just use a simple rigid box part on the ankle rather than building out separate toe chains, since boxes are simpler and still convey toe shapes while keeping proportions grounded near the floor.

Overall height comes to roughly 2.6 meters with horns included, which seems reasonable alongside the oversized hands hanging down near y=0.4. For the molten cracks, I'm planning to add glowing decals over the torso using an SVG crack texture with transparent cutouts, letting the glow effect apply to the decal so the seams read as emissive without needing extra geometry.

Now I'm placing separate crack decals for the chest/back and the limbs, drawn as orange-and-yellow stroked polylines, positioned on the torso's front and back surfaces with mirrored orientation. I'm also considering adding a glowing core sphere embedded in the chest, ringed by a gold torus, to give the lava-belly effect some visible depth.

For the basalt plating, I'm scattering flattened box/icosahedron shapes across the torso surface using a filter based on surface normal to avoid odd placement, embedding them slightly so the glowing seams show between plates. I'm picking a purple-toned basalt palette with darker shadow and lighter plate tones for the cel shading.

For the molten materials, I'm defining warm flat colors ranging from deep orange to pale yellow-white, plus a gold tone and dark ink for outlines, and considering a gradient paint to make the lower legs appear hotter near the base.

Now I'm planning glowing joint accents -- small spheres nested at the elbows, knees, and shoulders where parts meet, sized to peek out slightly from the limb geometry to suggest molten seams, with a separated shoulder pauldron to expose the joint glow.

Still planning seam colors and bands...

Defining the spine chain with four points and a radius function that tapers the torso width and depth smoothly from base to chest.

For the shoulders, I'm placing lumpy icosahedron pauldrons scaled unevenly, attached to the chest/arm bones, with glowing gold rim torii and jagged basalt spikes jutting off them as armor detail.

For the head, I'm using a flattened icosahedron parented to the head bone, positioned forward and up to follow the neck's curve so the head sits ahead of the torso rather than directly on top of it.

Now I'm sketching the face: a dark brow ridge box and slit-like glowing eyes placed symmetrically using local "left"/"right" offsets from the head joint, positioned forward and slightly above the head's center.

Checking the surface math, the eyes land right around forward 0.245, close enough to the skull surface that slightly protruding slit boxes will look fine without needing precise orientation. Moving on to the jaw joint, parented to the head at a forward offset.

Placing jaw joint position and aim using head-local coordinates, then sizing the jaw box relative to the jaw bone's own local frame. For the mouth interior I'm adding a small glow box between the jaws, and for teeth I'm thinking of using spike primitives anchored explicitly to the jaw bone, arranged in a ring along its top edge.

For the head ornamentation, I'm planning a basalt crest of tilted hex-prism columns plus a gold circlet band and hanging earring discs with red tassel sweeps, all genshin-style. On the back I'm clustering glowing hex-prism lava vents of varying heights anchored to the chest bone.

I'm skipping floating embers since nothing should hang detached above the body, keeping it minimal there instead. For gold trim I'm adding wristlet cuffs as oriented cylinder loops along the forearm direction, anchored to the arm joint.

I realize I can position these using the chain's frame at a given t-value, which already gives position and tangent orientation, so cylinders align along the limb naturally. I'll use this same frame approach for leg cuffs and the torso belt, placing the belt near the spine's midpoint and considering a torus with normal along the spine axis.

For the ring geometry, I'll build a torus and rotate it so its normal aligns with the local Y (tangent) direction, then scale it slightly to form an ellipse that matches the torso's cross-section. The torso belt ring radius needs to be at least as large as the body's cross-sectional radius at that point, plus maybe a secondary glowing ring just below it.

Now I'm working out the torso's radius formulas along the chain—rx and ry grow with parameter t—and checking that the belt's torus radius at t=0.2 sits snugly around the body's elliptical cross-section there, accounting for whether the ellipse width maps to x or z. I'm also sketching the pelvis as a scaled icosahedron at the hips.

I'm now designing the hanging loincloth armor: a tapered front plate with gold trim and a glowing rune, extruded from a trapezoid outline anchored to the hip bone, plus two side plates rotated to hang along the sides at an offset width.

I'm checking that the side plates clear the thigh geometry since the hip radius extends outward to roughly 0.5 in x, so I'm pushing the plate placement outward a bit so it sits over the leg like a proper armor cap rather than sinking into it.

Now I'm designing crack decal textures as SVG paths with jagged orange strokes and a thin yellow core, then figuring out how to place them on the torso front and back surfaces using a point/direction/size decal system, adjusting the z-depth so the "at" point lands near the actual surface.

I'm extending this decal placement logic to the arms and legs, choosing outward-facing directions and smaller sizes for the upper arm, forearm, thigh, and shin so the crack texture wraps naturally around each limb segment.

Now I'm thinking about adding a gold filigree ornament on the chest plate using a separate textured plane with transparent scroll patterns, positioning it just above the core on the torso's front surface and calculating the correct z-offset based on the chest radius.

Still placing shoulder gold accents...

Now I'm thinking through the bone chain naming for each arm side—shoulder, elbow, wrist joints with three points forming two spans, using a catmull curve for smooth limb geometry with an "arm" role, and setting up varying radii along the sweep for a tapered look.

Adjusting radii keyframes...

Checking elbow-to-hand distance fits the limb length, with the elbow spike angled backward reasonably. For hands, I'm deciding to build the palm as a rock-textured icosahedron near the wrist rather than doubling up fist and fingers, then planning a loop to generate four curling rock fingers hanging off the palm base.

Still writing finger chain code...

Still placing feet and toes geometry...

Checking overall height budget: hips at 1.05, chest to 2.0, pauldron radius 0.3 at 1.95, head center around 2.3, crest pushing total height to roughly 2.75m for this fantasy golem — a bit tall but acceptable, I'll verify scale later in the main pass. I'm setting the spine chain's starting joint to align with the hips at [0,1.05,0] rather than offsetting separately, keeping the parent-child relationship clean, and now moving to think through the torso's paint layers with mottled cel shading plus stuck-on plates.

I'm realizing I can get "basalt plates and molten seams" for free by reusing the same cell-based distance paint I used for seams elsewhere — wherever the gap between the two nearest cell edges is small, show glowing molten color, otherwise show rock texture. I'm writing a seamed-paint helper that takes a cell size and seam width, computes the voronoi-like distance difference, and returns either a core/hot molten color near seams or a rock color (using the cell's id to pick a shade variant) elsewhere — applying one consistent paint across torso, arms, legs, head, and pauldron so the plate pattern lines up seamlessly across the whole body, possibly adding extra chest-only decal cracks later if needed.

I'm scaling back the decal plan to just two SVGs — a filigree collar and a glowing rune emblem on the loin plate (using a separate glow-plane part rather than textures since extrusion only supports paint), dropping the crack decals entirely to keep things simpler. For the molten seam colors I'm just using flat bright "#ffd25a" and "#ff7b1c" values since cel-shading doesn't apply to emissive-style glow, and I'm filtering the torso plate-stick scatter to only appear where the surface normal's y is above -0.2.

Now I'm scattering small box-shaped plate sticks across the body — around 30 on the torso, 12 per arm, 10 per leg — each as its own part so they can individually take hit impacts from the sweep attacks, and I'm skipping an ink outline pass for now. I'm also building the seven back columns as six-sided cylinders anchored at the chest joint, each capped with a smaller glowing orange cylinder at the tip, positioning them in a fan spread across the x-axis behind the spine.

I'm adding a small crown of three columns on the head, a gold neck gorget as a short torus framed at the neck joint, and confirming the arm sweep starts correctly inside the shoulder pauldron. Now I'm considering giving the golem a mane of flame-card textures across the head and shoulders using SVG flame shapes.

Writing flame card code...

Still writing SVG gradient flame...

Drawing filigree path...

Now I'm designing a rune symbol for the loin plate, placing it as a glowing plane positioned at the front face of the pelvis armor, working out the exact z-offset so it sits just above the plate surface.

I'm checking that the plate placement clears the leg geometry given the hip joint radius and position, then setting the rune's vertical position near the top of the plate where it'll be most visible.

I'm also double-checking the color palette, confirming gold appears as a painted cel-shaded material rather than a flat-listed color string.

Now I'm sorting out which imports I actually need, settling on paint, cells, mottle utilities plus the toon and glow kits, then setting up the module's metadata export.

Writing import statements...

Defining more cell colors...

Still building the skeleton...

Still working out the neck chain...

Adding glowing eye boxes with slanted rotation, then planning a nose ridge, cheek spikes, and a jaw joint for the mouth structure.

Adding lower teeth spikes along the jaw and a faint glowing mouth gap, then starting on crown columns positioned around the head's top.

Still writing pillar helper...

Now I'm sketching the ear discs as gold cylinders at the head sides, then adding a tassel that sweeps downward from the ear point using a shrinking radius array and a red-gold color, plus a small gold bead at the tip to finish it off near the shoulder.

Next I'm placing flame-mane card frames along the back of the crown, seven of them spanning across the width, each angled outward with a backward flow and bend so they fan like flickering flames.

Then I'm mirroring smaller flame tufts near the shoulder pauldrons, attaching them to the arm's root joint once the arm skeleton exists. For the arms themselves, I'm building a loop over left and right sides, defining shoulder and hand anchor points and generating limb curves between them with a single bend direction to shape the arm sweep.

Building arm chain and mesh...

Still working out the gold rim placement...

Settling on R=0.32 with a thin tube for the torus band, so it hugs the surface without poking through. For the elbow, I'll add a small flattened icosahedron as a bone spike detail, and for the cuffs I'll place gold cylinder frames along the arm bone using the chain's `at(t)` positioning so they sit snug around the limb.

Now I'm building out the hand geometry: a flattened palm icosahedron, a few small claw spikes across the knuckles bound to the wrist bone, and a loop to generate four fingers with base, mid, and tip segments offset from the hand position.

Finishing finger chains...

Now I'm defining the thumb with its own base, mid, and tip positions offset from the hand, then adding scattered plate sticks across the arm surface using a surface scatter with minimum distance spacing.

For each plate hit, I'm attaching a small box geometry colored by cycling through the rock palette by index, with spin varying per iteration. I'm weighing whether to reuse a single plate geometry across iterations versus creating new boxes each time, since geometry cloning could matter for performance given the part budget.

Then I'm building the legs: computing hip and foot positions per side, creating a chain geometry through hip-knee-ankle control points, and sweeping it into a leg mesh with a polygonal cross-section, before adding knee details like a scaled icosphere for the kneecap and a gold cuff near the thigh.

Now I'm adding the shin cuff, foot box, and toe boxes with appropriate materials, plus a heel spike and a glowing ankle ring, then scattering plates along the leg and deciding to add loin plates front and back instead of side thigh armor.

For the loin plates, I'm positioning front and back pieces around the pelvis with gold outlines and darker inset plates underneath, mounted to the bone hips with a rune detail planned next.

Writing plate outline helper...

Then I'm thinking about a lava belt torus wrapping the waist, anchored to a spine frame around the hip area.

Planning more belt placements: gold at 0.16, hot ring at 0.08, another gold strap at 0.72, and adding a glowing core sphere on the chest front at the torso's upper position.

Still placing chest decorations...

Still placing bone columns...

Now I'm thinking about adding glowing rune textures and flame decals onto the armor plates, positioning a rune plane near the hips with proper texture mapping.

Sizing the gold waist plate against the pelvis and legs, checking clearances, and tallying up total part counts to make sure the sticks and other pieces stay in a reasonable range. I'm also double-checking the scatter filter so it only applies to the torso region correctly.

For the tassel, I'm defining a tapered sweep with varying radii and a reddish color, building helper points from the head joint's local coordinates, and setting up card frames and flame positions arranged in an arc around the crown.

Now I'm adding flame positions around each shoulder pauldron, spacing them with alternating offsets, and deciding to skip extra forearm drip effects since enough detail is covered. I'm finalizing the code, double-checking that all imports like the Joint type, frame, limb, rng, catmull, cells, mottle, paint, and svg are actually used.

I'm making sure INK and RUNE colors get referenced properly inside the fill and template strings, confirming THREE and FrameInput types are wired into the band helper, and sketching a ring geometry helper using a torus shape rotated to lie flat. I'm also working out the band function's color parameter, deciding to type it as either a string or a Paint object and importing the Paint type alongside the GOLD paint value.

I need to import cells, mottle, and paint along with the Paint type, then confirm the part() call applies the scale option correctly within the local frame orientation.
